routes.label: Count exterior unit squares in each face direction
Derive the exterior count from all cube faces and their joins

answerCheck.reason: The actual drawing shows three central cubes in a vertical stack, one attached to the right of its middle cube, and two in the lower-left chain. A matching unit-grid placement is (0,0,0),(0,0,1),(0,0,2),(1,0,1),(0,-1,0),(0,-2,0). There are five full-face joins: two vertical, one rightward and two along the lower chain. Each pair of joined faces is internal, whereas contacts only at an edge hide no surface area. Directly enumerating the six face directions gives 5,5,4,4,4,4 exposed unit squares, totaling 26, C, including hidden back and bottom faces. Alternatively six separate cubes contribute 36 unit faces and each of the five joins removes two, giving 6*6-2*5=26. Exact p161 and h110 cover simple cube/prism surfaces, not a universal assembly procedure. Clear that unsupported universal assessed claim and retain complete elementary OR routes from cube faces, component interpretation and unit surface area, with p112 local only to the mixed-operation cancellation route. The cancellation identity is derived for this explicit assembly; no new polycube synthesis scope or universal arithmetic method is asserted.
